question: Does a trained squared-ReLU toy differ from an independent-feature squared-ReLU control in boundary geometry or fixed-target corruption recovery?
scope: Post-hoc follow-up to known p≈4 geometry, not a blinded replication or a trained denoising model. New control/recovery outcomes are not used to tune this protocol.
control: 100→50→100, bias-free squared ReLU. One hidden unit per competent feature in ascending index order. Encoder coefficient equals the trained encoder-column norm; decoder coefficient matches the trained isolated positive unit-feature self-output. All other connections zero. No cross-feature computation; scalar clipping/squaring can itself suppress noise. Width and positive single-feature responses are matched, not trainable degrees of freedom or full off-axis behavior.

geometry.pair: first competence-conditioned pair in the saved trained-model plan
geometry.backgrounds: the same four frozen sparse backgrounds from the source report
geometry.response: L2 distance to each model's own clean output, median over four backgrounds; same original additive fitter and flags

corruption.values: signed Uniform(-1,1) when present, all 100 input dimensions
corruption.target: ReLU(clean x), held fixed as Gaussian input corruption varies
corruption.reference: ReLU(corrupted x): perform the original task on the corrupted input without restoring the clean input
corruption.oracle: f(clean x)+J(clean x)·noise; shares the natural model's clean output and first derivative. Has privileged clean-anchor access and is only a diagnostic ablation, not a deployable denoiser.
corruption.primary_outputs: the same 50 trained competent features for both networks and the reference
metrics: distance to each model's clean output

bootstrap.unit: clean example, keeping its four noise draws together

stopping_rule: One trained checkpoint, one analytic independent-feature control, one pair, three activity states, four small noise levels. No training, extra seeds, feature search, or expansion based on results. Save plots, all fits/flags, raw per-example error sums/counts and a short findings note.
